topic: Cobots: steered, non-driven wheels create virtual paths with almost no power (unicycle, scooter)
citation: Peshkin MA, Colgate JE, Wannasuphoprasit W, Moore CA, Gillespie RB, Akella P. Cobot architecture. IEEE Trans Robot Autom. 2001;17(4):377-390.
task_or_setup: Unicycle cobot: one free-rolling Rollerblade wheel, steering motor, no caster (steering axis through the contact point), force sensor at the handle; path mode (bilateral virtual surface) and free mode (steering nulls the operator's perpendicular force, eq. 2); Scooter: three steered wheels
participants_or_bench: Prototypes; operator trajectories shown (Fig. 3); no controlled user study with statistics
comparator: Brakes (joint brakes cannot render smooth arbitrary surfaces and dissipate energy); powered backdrivable robots
key_quantitative_findings: 'Virtual surface strength well over 100 pounds is attainable'; free mode 'qualitatively isotropic' 'at speeds of a few cm/s or faster'; 'noticeable hesitation as the wheels reorient' after a standstill; Scooter: speeds up to about 2 m/s comfortable; unrestricted steering angle found important (encoder wire wind-up).
units_and_conditions: Rollerblade wheels on a floor; payloads of several hundred pounds
locator: Sec. I.C (brakes), Sec. II.A-B and Fig. 1-3 (unicycle, eq. 1-2), Sec. III.A (Scooter)
limitations: Floor-scale devices; no handwriting; strength set by the wheel's skid limit, which is small for a pen (mu x 0.5 N)
relevance_to_design: The principle of the steered heel wheel: across-path force by the tyre's grip, along-path free; free mode by steering toward the writer's push; passive by construction
transferability_reason: Same kinematics and control laws; the skid limit and steering dynamics scale down with the pen
design_implication: Steer the heel wheel through its contact point; free mode by lateral-force nulling; expect hesitation at stroke starts and corners
search_query: WebSearch: Peshkin Colgate Cobot architecture IEEE Transactions 2001 pdf

topic: Position-correcting handheld tool: the user moves a frame coarsely, a stage moves the tool within 1/4 inch
citation: Rivers A, Moyer IE, Durand F. Position-correcting tools for 2D digital fabrication. ACM Trans Graph (SIGGRAPH). 2012;31(4):88.
task_or_setup: Handheld router/vinyl cutter/pen plotter; camera localisation on a marker map; eccentric-cam stage moves the tool; constant-speed and freeform path strategies
participants_or_bench: Device demonstrations and one plotted accuracy test
key_quantitative_findings: With location information a user keeps the tool within 1/8 in of the plan; stage range set to correct errors up to 1/4 in (1/2 in circle); plotted pattern (6 in wide): mean error 0.009 in, max 0.023 in.
units_and_conditions: inch; pen as the tool for the accuracy test
limitations: Not grounded force on the hand; the tool moves relative to the frame (like the Rev H nose); no user statistics
relevance_to_design: Macro-mini division: the hand (or the heel drive) does the gross path, a short-range stage (the nose) the detail
transferability_reason: Same division of labour; different scale and task
design_implication: Pair the heel drive (gross, grounded) with the nose (fine, +/-3 mm)

topic: Viscous damping loads reduce disabling action tremor (grounded energy-dissipating orthosis)
citation: Aisen ML, Arnold A, Baiges I, Maxwell S, Rosen M. The effect of mechanical damping loads on disabling action tremor. Neurology. 1993;43(7):1346-1350.
task_or_setup: Upper-extremity damping in three degrees of freedom by computer-controlled magnetic particle brakes (energy-dissipating orthoses)
participants_or_bench: 10 patients with cerebellar action tremor (multiple sclerosis or traumatic brain injury)
key_quantitative_findings: All patients had statistically and functionally significant tremor reduction with damping; rationale: damping opposes the high-velocity tremor more than slower voluntary motion.
units_and_conditions: Cerebellar tremor; damping values not in the abstract
limitations: Abstract only; cerebellar, not essential tremor; not handwriting; damping values unknown here
relevance_to_design: Grounded damping is the principle of the heel damper (ball) and the along-path brake
transferability_reason: Handwriting strokes are as fast as tremor, so damping discriminates less than in slow tasks
design_implication: Damp only above the writing band and measure the cost on clean writing (EXP-D09)
search_query: WebSearch + Europe PMC: effect of mechanical damping loads on disabling action tremor

topic: Wearable viscous tremor orthosis (Viscous Beam): damping constants achievable

limitations: Abstract only; wrist orthosis, not a pen
relevance_to_design: Order of magnitude of useful tremor damping, for comparison with the heel damper's 2-5 N s/m at the pen
design_implication: Heel damping of a few N s/m is small against the arm's own 11 N s/m (HAP-26): expect partial effects
